task1_blueprints.introduction_template: The line graph illustrates changes in [Topic] across [Country/Group] over a [X-year] period between [Year 1] and [Year 2].
task1_blueprints.overview_template: Overall, what stands out from the graph is that [Trend 1 experienced significant upward trajectory], whereas [Trend 2 witnessed a marked decline]. Furthermore, [Category X] consistently maintained the highest figures throughout the timeframe.
task1_blueprints.body_paragraph_tips: Group data logically by trends (upward vs downward), avoid listing every single year, prioritize highs, lows, plateaus, and points of intersection.

task1_blueprints.type: Static Comparison (Pie / Table at one point in time)
task1_blueprints.introduction_template: The pie charts compare the proportion of [Subject] allocated to [Categories] in [Year].
task1_blueprints.overview_template: Overall, it is immediately evident that [Category A] accounted for the vast majority of the total, while [Category B] constituted the least significant proportion.
task1_blueprints.body_paragraph_tips: Focus on proportions, ranks, ratios ('twice as much as', 'threefold', 'represented a negligible share').

structure: Paragraph 1: Paraphrase Prompt + Clear Thesis Statement (e.g. 'I wholeheartedly concur with this viewpoint because...')
Paragraph 2: First Strong Supporting Argument (Topic Sentence + Explanation + Concrete Example + Concluding link)
Paragraph 3: Second Supporting Argument or Counter-Perspective refutation
Paragraph 4: Conclusion (Restate position in different words + Forward-looking synthesis)

task2_blueprints.type: Discuss Both Views and Give Your Opinion
structure: Paragraph 1: Introduce debate + State which side you lean towards
Paragraph 2: Examine View A (Why proponents argue this + supporting merit)
Paragraph 3: Examine View B (Why opponents favor this + your primary rationale)
Paragraph 4: Synthesis conclusion firmly establishing your reasoned verdict
